_about: Materials a component is made of. cp J/(kg K), maxTemperatureC where the component fails, corrodedBy substance ids. formula is null for mixtures and composites. Rows carry the values the engine already used; maxTemperatureC is an engine failure limit (the melting point where a standard value exists), noted per row.

materials.name: Glass
materials.note: max is an engine failure limit for thermal shock and softening, not a standard constant

materials.name: Iron
materials.note: max is an engine failure limit below iron's melting point (1538 C)

materials.name: Wood
materials.note: max is an engine failure limit near the onset of pyrolysis

materials.name: Wall brick (LBNL)
materials.note: brick density 1920 kg/m3 and cp 790 from the LBNL library; max is an engine failure limit

materials.name: Brick
materials.note: max is an engine failure limit

materials.name: Flesh
materials.note: lumped body tissue: the IT'IS database lists soft tissues near 3400-3700; max is an engine failure limit (hyperthermia)

materials.name: Air (a room's)
materials.note: cp of dry air near 300 K; max is a sentinel meaning air does not fail
